public_rationale: The original March 2025 evaluation directly reports models claiming completion while expert graders identified substantive proof defects. That establishes the modest claim that this sometimes happens. It supports a failure to catch errors in delivered work, without establishing what internal checking the models attempted.
limitations: The evidence concerns difficult Olympiad proofs and the tested model versions.
It does not establish a failure rate across ordinary questions or later models.
The severity judgment is not independently scored.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is behavioral: models sometimes present materially flawed proofs as completed solutions.
Failure to sanity-check means that errors remain undetected or uncorrected in the delivered answer. It does not establish that no internal checking was attempted.
Deeply problematic is an evaluative judgment and is not separately scored.
The surrounding discussion concerns the March 2025 USAMO evaluation. I use March 2025 as the latest completed monthly observation period before the post.
